_meta.goal: make agentflow's specs + test pyramid a real contract (archive specs, traceability, contract tests, scope enforcement, run.rs units, CI clippy)

tasks.title: Archive all 5 openspec changes into a living spec library at openspec/specs/ (reconcile the broken delta headers so `openspec validate --specs` passes)
tasks.accept: test -f openspec/specs/state/spec.md && test -z "$(ls openspec/changes | grep -v '^archive$')" && openspec validate --specs && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: agentflow has 5 openspec changes marked Complete but NO living spec library (`openspec list --specs` prints 'No specs found'). Archive all 5 so `openspec/specs/<id>/spec.md` becomes the authoritative contract.

Use the CLI: `openspec archive <name> --yes`. It applies the change's delta to the main spec library and moves the change to `openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<name>/`. It ABORTS ATOMICALLY on a bad delta and prints a precise reason — iterate until every archive succeeds.

KNOWN-BAD DELTAS (already diagnosed — these are why a blind loop fails). Fix exactly these:
  1. ORDER: archive `rust-orchestrator` FIRST (it is the base: it ADDs the initial requirements), then `agent-sandboxing`.
  2. openspec/changes/multi-repo/specs/worktree/spec.md — it has `## MODIFIED Requirements` for 'Worktrees target the task's repository' and 'Self-heal spans all repositories', headers that do NOT exist in the base worktree spec. These are genuinely NEW requirements: change the section to `## ADDED Requirements`.
  3. openspec/changes/worker-routing/specs/cli/spec.md — `## MODIFIED 'Cost report'` does not exist in the base cli spec. It is new: change the section to `## ADDED Requirements`.
  4. openspec/changes/retry-context/specs/lifecycle/spec.md — MODIFIED 'Prompt rendering'. The archive REFUSES a MODIFIED block that drops scenarios already in the library: you must preserve the existing scenario 'template substitution' inside the modified block (keep the base scenario text verbatim, alongside the two new retry scenarios).
  5. 'Cost receipts' (state) is MODIFIED by BOTH worker-routing and retry-context. Archive worker-routing FIRST, then make retry-context's block a COMPLETE replacement that contains the union: the base scenarios ('receipt appended per attempt', 'cost aggregates receipts'), worker-routing's additions ('failed attempts are recorded', 'legacy receipts stay loadable'), PLUS retry-context's own ('failed receipt carries the reason', 'legacy receipts parse with no error'). Merge the requirement prose too (outcome + error fields in one paragraph). If you archive retry-context first, mirror the change.

A MODIFIED block is a REPLACEMENT, not a patch: it must reproduce every scenario that should survive.

DONE when: `openspec list --specs` shows 7 specs (cli, config, lifecycle, sandbox, scheduling, state, worktree); `openspec validate --specs` reports 7 passed / 0 failed; `openspec/changes/` contains ONLY `archive/`; and the git tree is committed. Do NOT delete spec content to make validation pass — reconcile it. Keep the full Rust suite green.

tasks.title: Add out_of_scope_edit_fails_the_attempt — enforce task.scope on the agent's diff (today scope is prompt-only and never checked)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn out_of_scope_edit_fails_the_attempt' tests/scope_enforcement.rs && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: `task.scope` is currently only a sentence in the prompt ('Do not touch files outside the allowed scope') — nothing checks it, so an agent can edit anything. Make it an enforced contract.

1. src/execute.rs: after the agent exits successfully and its change is committed on the attempt branch, compute the files the attempt changed, e.g. `git -C <worktree> diff --name-only <base_branch>...HEAD` (base branch = the branch the worktree was cut from; use the existing git helper in the module).
   - An empty `task.scope` means 'any file' (current semantics — keep it).
   - Otherwise every changed path MUST match at least one scope entry, using the SAME matcher the scheduler uses: `crate::scheduler::scope_overlap(changed_path, scope_entry)` (prefix/glob-prefix match). Reuse it; do not write a second matcher.
   - On violation: fail the attempt with an error whose message contains 'out of scope' and names the offending paths, e.g. `attempt edited files outside task scope: src/other.rs (allowed: src/execute.rs)`. The violation must happen BEFORE merging, so the offending change never reaches the base branch.
   - Exempt nothing by default; keep it strict.
2. tests/scope_enforcement.rs — model it on tests/e2e.rs (`fixture`, `worker_json`, `gate_cmd`, the `example_agent` binary):
   - `#[test] fn out_of_scope_edit_fails_the_attempt()`: one task with scope `["in_scope.txt"]`; drive `example_agent` with FAKE_AGENT_TOUCH=out_of_scope.txt (remember it must ride TF_AGENT_ENV_PASSTHROUGH); assert run::run_loop reports the task Failed, `last_error` mentions 'out of scope', and out_of_scope.txt was NOT merged into the base repo.
   - `#[test] fn in_scope_edit_is_merged()`: scope `["in_scope.txt"]`, FAKE_AGENT_TOUCH=in_scope.txt -> task Done and the file exists in the base repo (proves you did not break the happy path).
Keep the FULL suite green — many existing e2e tests use FAKE_AGENT_TOUCH, so check their scopes still pass (if an existing test writes a file outside its declared scope, that test's fixture scope must be widened, and say so in the commit message).

tasks.title: Add clippy to the CI test job — CI currently runs only fmt + test, so clippy drift is invisible
tasks.accept: grep -q 'cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings' .github/workflows/ci.yml && python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))" && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: .github/workflows/ci.yml's `test` job runs `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test --all-targets` but NOT clippy, so clippy warnings (round 2 found 13) are invisible to CI. agentflow's own gates run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, so CI must enforce the same bar.

1. In the `test` job, ensure the toolchain installs clippy (e.g. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with `with: components: clippy`) and add a step running EXACTLY:
     cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   Place it before the test step so warnings fail fast.
2. Keep the existing `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test --all-targets` steps. Do not remove the coverage job.
3. The YAML must stay valid (`python3 -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"`), and keep the existing comments explaining that E2E needs no network/LLM keys.
The gate greps for the exact clippy command and re-runs the full local suite.

tasks.title: Add every_requirement_has_at_least_one_referencing_test — a spec<->test traceability checker so the new spec library is a contract, not prose
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn every_requirement_has_at_least_one_referencing_test' tests/spec_traceability.rs && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: `openspec/specs/<id>/spec.md` is now the living contract (see the archived specs). Nothing links those requirements to tests, so nobody can answer 'which requirement is unverified?'. Add that check.

MARKER CONVENTION (document it in docs/spec-traceability.md): a test that verifies a requirement carries a comment line
    // spec: <spec-id>/<requirement-slug>
immediately above the `#[test]` fn. Slug = the requirement title lowercased, with every run of non-alphanumeric characters replaced by a single '-' and trimmed, e.g. `### Requirement: Cost receipts` -> `state/cost-receipts`, `### Requirement: Scope contention avoidance` -> `scheduling/scope-contention-avoidance`.

1. tests/spec_traceability.rs:
   - Parse every `openspec/specs/*/spec.md`, extract each `### Requirement:` title -> `<spec-id>/<slug>`.
   - Walk the repo's test sources (tests/*.rs and src/**/*.rs) for `spec: <id>/<slug>` markers.
   - `#[test] fn every_requirement_has_at_least_one_referencing_test()`: FAIL listing every requirement with no marker, with an actionable message naming the requirement and the expected marker text.
   - `#[test] fn traceability_allowlist_stays_small()`: a small, explicitly-documented `const UNMAPPED: &[(&str, &str)]` of (requirement, reason) for requirements that genuinely cannot be tested yet; assert `UNMAPPED.len() <= 3` so the gap can only shrink. Do NOT use UNMAPPED to paper over requirements that have an obvious test.
   - Sanity-check the checker itself: include a test that a deliberately-bogus requirement fails the matcher logic.
2. Add the `// spec: ...` markers to the EXISTING tests that cover these requirements (you may also add new small tests where a requirement clearly has none). Map by reading the spec text: config loading -> config tests, worktree lifecycle/merge serialization -> worktree tests + tests/e2e.rs, scope contention -> scheduler tests, status persistence / cost receipts -> state tests, prompt rendering -> execute prompt tests, agent env allowlist -> execute/e2e env tests, run/status/cost/clean/validate commands -> tests/cli.rs, resume & self-heal -> tests/journal.rs, sandbox wrapper hook -> sandbox tests.
3. Adding a comment above an existing test is a no-op for behavior; keep the full suite green. No new dependencies.
4. Requires the spec library from r4-spec-archive to exist — do not edit openspec/ (it is not in your scope).
